To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the probe design and performance is suitable for 1H-decoupled 31P-MRSI studies at 1.6 T and that the probe design is suitable for 31P-MR spectroscopy and spectroscopic imaging studies of the head and upper torso region at 1.2 and 1.6 Tesla.
the probe has been successfully tested in 31P MRT studies in 15 volunteers and 5 patients and that the results are in agreement with those obtained with a commercial 31P probe.
a compact 1H/31P double resonant probe was designed, evaluated and validated that enables 1H decouple 31P MARS studies of the head and/or neck.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a radio-frequency probe for the acquisition of 1H-decoupled 31P MR spectroscopy data at 1. 5 Tesla.
the development of a new probe that is capable of providing high-quality spectra of the phosphorous-containing compounds of interest in the head and neck.
the design, construction and evaluation of a new radio-frequency probe for the 31P MRT of the head and the neck region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probe has been designed and tested to be a safe and reliable tool for 1H-decoupled 31P spectroscopic studies of human subjects at 1.0 T.
the probe is suitable for 1H-decoupled 31P-MRS in vivo studies of the head and the neck.
the 1H-31P double-resonant RF probe for 1.5 T is a versatile and compact device that can be applied for 31P MMR studies in the head and neck regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to design and build a probe that meets all the requirements for 1H-decoupled 31P-MRSI at 1. 5T.
we have developed a probe for 1 H decoupled 1 3 1 P MRS at 4.7 T, which is a versatile and compact design.
this probe is a very useful tool to study 31P metabolism in the head and neck, but also in the brain, breast, liver and kidney.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of a double resonated surface coil for MRS can be optimized for a specific application by careful consideration of the geometry of the coil and the RF properties of the sample.
a double resonator probe for 1.5 T is feasible and that it can be designed to be compact, robust and versatile.
a compact double-resonant 1H-31P probe can be used in the head and neck to obtain high quality 1H decouple 31P spectra.
